title: the zoning blocker was false; the join under all four leaves was not
mergeSha: not applicable: lane instructed not to merge
snapshotDeclared: code: legacy-design-tools, branch fix/ctx-b7-claim-vs-roll-leaves, commit e7282112, cut from origin/main 9ae49246. data: Neon project fancy-fire-06136146, branch f06-staging-neondb, database neondb, every scan read-only with default_transaction_read_only=on, between 2026-09-10T15:03Z and 15:40Z.
missionPremise: CTX-B6 (PR #651, merged as 9ae49246) established roll-over-claim precedence for baseFacts.situsAddress and deliberately left three siblings recoverable from the same already-loaded declared-vintage row: acreage 103,913 cells, situsCity 78,428, situsZip 17,674. It left them because it judged that situsCity feeds resolveZoningJurisdiction and would move zoning-jurisdiction assignment for roughly 78,000 parcels, which was too large to slip into a card about a different leaf. This card exists to decide, per leaf, whether B6's precedence is right, and to state what situsCity moves if it is.
completionPredicate: A stranger can evaluate this by running, from this branch, in artifacts/api-server: (1) `npx tsx src/ctxB6VerifySitusAddressCli.ts --self-test` -> failures=0, exit 0, and the log must show the gate asserted in BOTH directions on identical inputs; (2) `DATABASE_URL=<staging read-only> npx tsx src/ctxB6VerifySitusAddressCli.ts --grade-stored` -> exit 1 (the BEFORE run); (3) the same without --grade-stored -> 16/16 PASS, exit 0, including four Hays parcels graded `gate-refused-keeps-claim`; (4) `--violate` -> exit 1; (5) `DATABASE_URL=postgres://u:p@127.0.0.1:5432/none npx vitest run src/nodeFacetBakeTier1Conformant.test.ts` -> 122/122; (6) flipping `case "zip-conflict": return false` to `return true` in declaredRollMayOverride makes 5 of those tests fail with exit 1. Every count in this close carries its counting rule and can be re-derived from the SQL in the heavyScans section.
scopeBasis: legacy-design-tools only, per the dispatch. hauska-factory, hauska-engine and hauska-map were not touched. lib/cad-ingest and lib/db live INSIDE this repo (lib/cad-ingest/src/txgio/zoning-layers.ts, zoning-stamp-db.ts, vintage.ts) and were READ, not written -- the zoning registry's elgin-tx record-key inconsistency is flagged and deliberately not fixed because it is a zoning-registry concern rather than a tier-1 bake one. txgio_parcel and cad_property were read only. The dollar path (fetchCountyCadPropertyRoll -> baseFacts.cadRoll) was deliberately NOT gated even though this card proves it carries the same defect, because changing what cadRoll reports on 29,404 live rows is a separate card with a separate blast radius. No deploy, no Cloud Build, no Cloud Run job, no bake, publish or walk.

theQuestionThisCardExistedToAnswer.question: Whether the roll-over-claim precedence CTX-B6 established for situsAddress is right for situsCity, situsZip and acreage, and what it moves if it is.
theQuestionThisCardExistedToAnswer.answer: It is right for situsCity and situsZip and NOT right, as stated, for acreage. And CTX-B6's stated reason for leaving situsCity -- the zoning-jurisdiction coupling -- is FALSE. The real obstacle was somewhere else entirely, it applies to all four leaves including the one B6 already merged, and it is that the prop_id join underneath the precedence is not sound on one of the six counties.

situsCity.detail: 78,428 gains (claim silent, roll speaks) and 30,841 swaps (both speak, differ). Under the gate: 78,360 gains taken, 1,219 swaps taken, 29,621 swaps refused. Zero parcels lose a city in any scenario.

situsZip.detail: 17,674 recoverable absences plus 29,949 disagreements. Only consumer outside the bake and assembler is lib/smartSiteStub.ts:179 (composeSitusLabel) -- display only, no routing, no gate, no join key, no jurisdiction. situsZip is ALSO the gate's corroborator, which is not circular: on corroboration the roll ZIP equals the claim ZIP so the write is a no-op or a +4 refinement, on conflict the claim is kept, and on a gain there is no claim ZIP to contradict.

acreage.disposition: IMPLEMENTED with a DIFFERENT precedence, deliberately not B6's
acreage.detail: Acreage has THREE sources and one of them is a MEASUREMENT. The parcel-join ring is a shoelace on this parcel's own geometry; the roll cell and the claim cell are transcriptions. The ring keeps precedence over both, so cad_property.land_acres slots BELOW the ring and ABOVE the claim, under its own method string `cad-roll-declared-land-acres`. Applying roll-over-claim verbatim would have put a transcribed roll cell above a measured ring, which is a different and worse defect than the one being fixed.

situsAddress_retrofitted.disposition: GATE RETROFITTED onto CTX-B6's merged rule
situsAddress_retrofitted.detail: Not in the dispatch's scope list and it is the single most consequential change here. See theFindingWorthMoreThanTheFix below.

answer1_theZoningBlockerIsFalse.verdict: ZERO parcels change zoning jurisdiction. Not few -- zero, in every county, for a structural reason.

codeRead: resolveZoningJurisdiction (lib/cad-ingest/src/txgio/zoning-layers.ts:571-575) consults situsCity ONLY when txgio_parcel.zoning_jurisdiction is blank; a stamped-but-unknown key still returns before situs is read.

assembleTier1Payload (artifacts/api-server/src/lib/nodeFacetTier1Assemble.ts:350-384) writes the zoning facet -- the only place jurisdictionKey survives onto a payload -- ONLY when zoning_district is non-blank.
The single writer of either column, flushBatch in lib/cad-ingest/src/txgio/zoning-stamp-db.ts:139-141, sets zoning_district AND zoning_jurisdiction in ONE UPDATE statement.

The only other writer, artifacts/api-server/scripts/backfill-bastrop-tier1-zoning-provenance.mjs:131-137, only ever FILLS a missing jurisdiction WHERE a district exists -- it narrows the gap, never widens it.
Therefore a district without a jurisdiction is unwritable, and where a district exists the situs fallback is unreachable.

measurement.denominator: 1,568,849 txgio_parcel rows in the six CTX counties. Full scan, no sampling.
measurement.countingRule: nullif(btrim(coalesce(col,'')),'') IS NOT NULL per column, one row per txgio_parcel row.

endToEndConfirmation.rule: applied the actual precedence to all 1,516,110 stored tier-1 rows and counted changed cities landing on a parcel that is unstamped AND carries a district

provenTwoWays.secondMechanismConsideredAndRejected: the co-presence could be a coincidence of the current stamp run rather than a property of the writer. Rejected by READING the writer: one UPDATE sets both columns. A future writer that set only one WOULD reach the fallback, so the situs fallback is unreachable-today rather than dead, and that distinction is recorded in the code comment rather than collapsed.

answer1_theZoningBlockerIsFalse.consequence: the coupling that blocked CTX-B6 does not exist. The onSitusFallback callback still fires and the bake still logs it, but its result cannot reach a served zoning jurisdiction on this data.

answer2_directionBreakdown.denominatorRule: every place_layer_snapshots row with adapter_key='node-facets:tier1' whose place_key second segment is one of 48021, 48055, 48209, 48309, 48453, 48491. Full scan.
answer2_directionBreakdown.countingRule: claim city = the stored baseFacts.situsCity when it is a STRING (an earned-absence object counts as no city). new city = retired ? claim : coalesce(declared-roll situs_city, claim). changed = new IS DISTINCT FROM claim, case- and whitespace-sensitive.
answer2_directionBreakdown.whyLossIsStructurallyZero: a blank roll cell falls through to the claim. 1,676 Hays parcels carry a claim city where the declared roll's own cell is empty, and every one keeps its city. This is the falsifier CP1 pre-registered as 'what would prove the whole card wrong', and it came back clean.
answer2_directionBreakdown.doAnyCurrentlyServeAZoningDistrictThatWo: NO. 67,355 changed parcels do carry a stamp and therefore a district, but the stamp is a point-in-polygon determination against the city's own zoning polygon layer -- derived from geometry, never from situsCity. A changed situsCity cannot make a stamp wrong because the stamp never depended on it, and the jurisdictionKey served for those parcels comes from the stamp. The remaining 41,914 changers carry no district at all.

answer3_correctionOrRegression.instrument: MEANING-SHAPED, not internal consistency. Input A: txgio_parcel.zoning_jurisdiction, a PIP determination against the city's own zoning polygon layer -- derived from GEOMETRY. Input B: the situs city, a transcription on a CAD roll row. One party cannot satisfy both sides. Measured for the claim's city and the roll's city over the SAME stamped parcels; whichever agrees with geometry more often is the better source.
answer3_correctionOrRegression.denominator: 533,391 stamped parcels across the six counties
answer3_correctionOrRegression.countingRule: agreement = the normalised situs city equals the stamped layer's normalised cityName or contains it -- the same normalisation resolveZoningJurisdiction itself uses (lowercase, non-alphanumerics to single spaces, trim).

48491.note: situsCity is absent on all 158,867 stamped Williamson parcels, so neither source agrees with anything. Recorded rather than read as a tie.

answer3_correctionOrRegression.theHeadlineWouldHaveLicensedTheWrongChan: a net +38,696 across six counties conceals a -12,323 on one. DEV_PROCESS 1.1: the figure had to travel with its per-county split. Taking the six-county number alone would have shipped the Hays regression.

theFindingWorthMoreThanTheFix.name: the prop_id join under all four roll-preferring leaves is not sound on Hays, and CTX-B6's merged rule is already exposed to it
theFindingWorthMoreThanTheFix.howItSurfaced: the Hays swaps are not a vintage correction. They are a near-symmetric all-pairs permutation across every city in the county: SAN MARCOS->KYLE 2,268 beside KYLE->SAN MARCOS 1,641; BUDA->KYLE 1,914 beside KYLE->BUDA 1,722; DRIPPING SPRINGS->KYLE 1,545 beside KYLE->DRIPPING SPRINGS 1,017. A genuine annexation-driven correction is overwhelmingly ONE-directional. A symmetric scramble is a KEY COLLISION.
theFindingWorthMoreThanTheFix.theDiscriminator: the 5-digit situs ZIP, compared between the 2025 and 2026 cad_property rows on the SAME prop_id. Neither vintage formats a ZIP differently, so a differently-transcribed street proves nothing while a different ZIP proves a different parcel. Two independently derived values on the same key.

crossVintagePropIdStability.countingRule: cad_property tax_year 2025 JOIN cad_property tax_year 2026 on (county_fips, prop_id), restricted to pairs where BOTH rows carry a non-blank situs_zip; agreement on left(btrim(situs_zip),5).

theFindingWorthMoreThanTheFix.threeIndependentFieldsConverge: Hays cross-vintage agreement measured separately on ZIP (53.86%), on situs city (53.2%) and on the normalised street segment (~52%). Three different fields, three separate queries, one number.

andTheClaimIsAPerfectCopyOfItsOwnVintage.read: each claim agrees with its OWN vintage 100.00% and with the other ~52%. The disagreement is entirely cross-vintage. That is prop_id RENUMBERING, which buildRecordRetirement's own basis text already names: split, merged, renumbered or removed.

theFindingWorthMoreThanTheFix.corroborationFromTheCodebaseItself: 48209 and 48491 are the two entries in LANDUSE_JOIN_DISABLED_FIPS_SEED (artifacts/api-server/src/lib/joinNormalize.ts:73-76), gate-blocked because 'a CAD prop_id joined into a divergent TxGIO numbering attaches another parcel's zoning stamp and geometry'. The program already knew Hays prop_ids are unstable ACROSS SOURCES; nobody applied it to the CAD-to-CAD join ACROSS VINTAGES, which is the same failure with the same key.

exposureOfCTX_B6sMERGEDRule.mechanism: resolveConformantSitusAddress as merged states 'the roll wins even over a usable claim', unconditionally. On a renumbered prop_id that writes ANOTHER PARCEL'S street over a correct one.
exposureOfCTX_B6sMERGEDRule.countingRule: stored tier-1 rows where the claim carries a street (something alphanumeric before the first comma) AND the declared-roll row carries a DIFFERENT street on the normalised street segment; the second figure further restricts to rows whose claim ZIP and declared-roll ZIP are both present and differ.
exposureOfCTX_B6sMERGEDRule.read: B6's rule is RIGHT for Travis (99.73% key-stable; its 14,431 swaps are the StratMap-vs-PACS formatting difference on the SAME parcel, only 67 on a conflicting ZIP) and WRONG for Hays (29,395 of 37,503 swaps land on a row the ZIP proves is a different parcel).
exposureOfCTX_B6sMERGEDRule.timing: B6's own close records that the store is unchanged and its fix appears when the integration seat re-bakes. THE DEFECT HAS NOT WRITTEN YET. This card catches it in the only cheap window it was ever going to have.

theFindingWorthMoreThanTheFix.aConvenientResultIDidNotTrust: the same cross-vintage test on Travis situs_address returned ZERO exact-string agreement in BOTH directions, which reads as a catastrophic key failure in already-merged work. It is not. Re-measured on a normalised street key it is 53.9%, and on the ZIP 99.73%. The zero was a FORMATTING difference between the 2025 StratMap drop and the 2026 PACS export (48453:224793 is ', TX 78756' at 2025 and '4709 SHOALWOOD AVE' at 2026, ZIP 78756 both years). Reporting the exact-string zero would have been a confident wrong claim about merged work, and it looked like a finding.

theDesignShipped.rule: prefer the declared roll only where the row is CORROBORATED as the same parcel; otherwise keep the claim.
theDesignShipped.costsNoQuery: the claim already carries situsZip and the declared row already carries situs_zip, and both are already loaded for the dollar path. No county-level threshold, no tuned constant, no allowlist to go stale.

fiveStates.no-roll-row: retired (CTX-RETIRE). Keep the claim, ungated. Reached FIRST everywhere, proven by test.
fiveStates.same-vintage: claim taxYear == declared taxYear, so it is literally the same row. Prefer.
fiveStates.zip-corroborated: both ZIPs present and equal (5-digit, so ZIP+4 and spacing are not conflicts). Prefer.
fiveStates.zip-conflict: both ZIPs present and different. REFUSE, keep the claim, RECORD what was refused.
fiveStates.uncorroborated: one or both ZIPs absent. Nothing established either way.

theDesignShipped.theAsymmetryIsTheRule: a GAIN converts an absence into data: nothing usable is destroyed and ENFORCEMENT's inverse of ruling A1 positively requires it, so it is taken unless the ZIP actively contradicts the row. A SWAP converts data into other data, and on an unverified key that means another parcel's data over a value that is currently correct for its own vintage. So a swap is taken ONLY on positive corroboration. 'Nothing was established' is not a licence to overwrite.

measuredEffect.countingRule: each stored tier-1 row classified into exactly one trust state, then cross-tabbed against whether the city change is a gain (claim silent) or a swap (both present, differ).
measuredEffect.theShape: 95.6% of all swaps (29,472 of 30,840) sit on a zip-conflict row. The swap population and the key-collision population are very nearly the same set, which is the number telling you what the population IS rather than a rule fitted to a number.

answer4_acreage_theDispatchsOwnQuestion.question: how many of the 103,913 are currently served as `refused` versus bare null, per county
answer4_acreage_theDispatchsOwnQuestion.answer: ALL 103,913 ARE REFUSED. ZERO ARE BARE NULL. In every county.
answer4_acreage_theDispatchsOwnQuestion.countingRule: acreage leaf classified on the STORED payload: an object carrying 'value' is resolved, an object with status='absent' is an absence (verdict refused vs absent-verified), a bare JSON null is a bare null. Recoverable = the declared-vintage cad_property row carries land_acres > 0.
answer4_acreage_theDispatchsOwnQuestion.theFinding: the program serves a DECLARED REFUSAL -- verdict 'refused', lookupVerdict 'lookup-failed', basis 'geometry was never looked up for this parcel, unmeasured, not verified absent, and the claim carries no landAcres' -- on 103,913 parcels whose declared-vintage roll holds a usable land_acres, in the same row the payload's dollars already come from. CTX-LEAVES2's basis is literally true about the two sources it names and materially false about the parcel, because a third source was never consulted. A refusal over recoverable data is worse than a bare null: a bare null is visibly unfinished, and a refusal reads as a finding.
answer4_acreage_theDispatchsOwnQuestion.andBastropIsTheDispatchsWorkedExample: the dispatch names a 2026-09-10 re-bake that wrote 15,542 Bastrop rows as refused. Confirmed at source: 15,542 refused, of which 1,598 are recoverable. The re-bake has in fact landed across ALL six counties, not just Bastrop -- there is not one bare-null acreage cell left anywhere in the corpus.

whereIStoppedAtARulingBoundary.whyItIsARulingAndNotAnEngineeringJudgeme: the fix is not a leaf. It is one of: re-declare 48209's vintage to 2025; re-acquire a 2026 Hays roll together with a prop_id crosswalk; or extend this card's per-parcel gate to the dollar path. Each has a different cost, a different owner and a different blast radius across money-facing fields that are live now. Choosing among them is not this card's call.

instrumentDefectInTheInheritedInstrument.defect: the instrument synthesised the CLAIM's situsCity and situsZip FROM THE DECLARED ROLL. Harmless for CTX-B6, whose leaf was situsAddress. Fatal for CTX-B7: it would have made claim and roll agree BY CONSTRUCTION on exactly the two leaves being decided, so every before/after would have shown no movement -- and it would have made the same-parcel gate read `zip-corroborated` on every parcel, including the 29,404 whose ZIPs actually conflict.

instrumentDefectInTheInheritedInstrument.howItWasFound: by reading the instrument before running it. The wrong version would have PASSED, and its result would have been 'nothing moves, close the card'.

whatRemainsOpen: The store is unchanged. This PR fixes the WRITER. The 78,360 city recoveries, 17,674 ZIP recoveries and 103,913 acreage recoveries appear only when the integration seat re-bakes and re-publishes; so does the protection of the 29,539 streets and 29,472 cities the gate refuses.

Re-baking rewrites the basis text of existing situsCity/situsZip and acreage absences, because they now name the declared roll as a second searched source. Harmless byte change to already-correct rows, declared so nobody reads it as a regression in a diff.

The `uncorroborated` residue is the one judgement in the gate that is a judgement: 14,381 gains taken without corroboration (14,285 Travis, 63 Caldwell, 33 Hays) and 241 Hays swaps refused without corroboration. Travis is 99.73% key-stable so its gains are safe; the design errs toward recovery on gains and refusal on swaps, and that asymmetry is stated in the code and pinned by a test.

leave_behind.detail: live code with a live logging callback that cannot reach a served zoning jurisdiction, because zoning_district and zoning_jurisdiction are co-written by one UPDATE. Not dead -- a future writer that set only one column would reach it -- but nothing today does. Worth either retiring with a decline test or keeping with a comment saying it is a guard against a writer that does not exist yet. Named rather than removed because removing live code on a measurement is the shape this program warns about.

The cityName matches so it resolves to the same string today. Recommend making the lookup key-by-value, or renaming so record key equals cityKey. Flagged, not fixed: zoning-registry scope, not tier-1 bake scope.

That makes the naming hazard worse, not better: a future reader who takes it for the declared vintage will now also mis-gate. The code comment at its assignment says so.

lessonsForFleetMemory.text: A CARD'S STATED BLOCKER IS A CLAIM, NOT A PREMISE. CTX-B7 existed because CTX-B6 judged that situsCity moves zoning jurisdiction for ~78,000 parcels. It moves zero. The disproof took two code reads and one cross-tab and would have taken twenty minutes at any point in B6. Check the blocker before you build around it.

Reachability is decided by the WRITER, not by the reader. zoning_district and zoning_jurisdiction are always co-present because one UPDATE (cad-ingest zoning-stamp-db.ts flushBatch) sets both, which makes the situsCity fallback in resolveZoningJurisdiction unreachable wherever a zoning facet exists. Measuring the columns showed the correlation; reading the writer showed it is structural rather than incidental.

A roll-over-claim preference is only as sound as the KEY it joins on. Cross-vintage cad_property prop_id stability, tested on the situs ZIP (a field neither vintage formats): Travis 99.73%, Caldwell 99.21%, HAYS 53.86%. On Hays a prop_id names a different parcel in 2025 than in 2026, so any join from a 2025-vintage claim to the 2026 declared roll attaches another parcel's data.

A near-symmetric all-pairs permutation is a KEY COLLISION signature, not a correction. Hays situsCity showed SAN MARCOS->KYLE 2,268 beside KYLE->SAN MARCOS 1,641 and every other ordered pair in both directions. A real annexation is one-directional. Read the SHAPE of a disagreement before reading its size.

Pick a discriminator the two sources cannot format differently. Comparing Travis street addresses across vintages gave ZERO exact-string agreement (catastrophic-looking) and 53.9% normalised (alarming) and 99.73% on the ZIP (fine). The ZIP was right because StratMap and PACS transcribe streets differently and neither reformats a 5-digit ZIP. A convenient-looking catastrophic result is still a reason to distrust the instrument.

When a preference can be wrong, gate it on a corroborator you ALREADY HAVE rather than on a threshold. The claim carries situsZip and the declared row carries situs_zip and both were already loaded, so the same-parcel gate costs no query, no tuned constant and no allowlist. A county-level threshold would have needed a number nobody could defend.

GAIN and SWAP are different risks and deserve different rules. Filling an absence from an uncorroborated source destroys nothing; overwriting a value from an uncorroborated source writes another parcel's data over a correct one. Symmetric rules on asymmetric risks either refuse 78,428 legitimate recoveries or accept 29,621 wrong overwrites.

A REFUSAL OVER RECOVERABLE DATA IS WORSE THAN A BARE NULL. All 103,913 recoverable acreage cells are served as verdict 'refused' and zero as bare nulls. A null is visibly unfinished; a refusal reads as a finding and closes the question. Watch for refusal counts that look like completed work.

THE SCOPE OF AN ABSENCE IS PART OF THE ABSENCE. claimLeafAbsence said 'the claim was read and carries no situsCity' while cad_property had never been consulted -- literally true, materially false about the parcel. That sentence is why 78,428 recoverable cities survived six consecutive leaf audits looking like finished work.

Do not apply a sibling's precedence rule without asking what KIND of value each source is. situsAddress/City/Zip are all transcriptions, so preferring the payload's own vintage is strictly right. Acreage has a MEASUREMENT (the parcel ring) among its sources, and putting a transcribed roll cell above it would have been a worse defect than the one being fixed.

An inherited instrument must be READ before it is reused, and its defects are scoped to the question it was built for. ctxB6VerifySitusAddressCli synthesised the claim's situsCity and situsZip from the declared roll -- harmless for B6's leaf, fatal for B7's, and the wrong version would have PASSED and reported 'nothing moves'.

Of the changers 67,355 are already stamped and 0 are unstamped-with-a-district, so zero zoning jurisdictions move.

Per county recoverable: Travis 67,915, Williamson 16,927, Hays 14,796, Caldwell 2,677, Bastrop 1,598, McLennan 0. The CTX-LEAVES2 re-bake has landed in all six counties, not just Bastrop.

Travis 0.28% and Caldwell 0.80% are the real ZIP-churn baseline; Hays at 45.4% is 160x it. SHIPPED AND SERVING.

2026-09-10, staging: CTX-B6's merged rule would replace a usable claim street with a different roll street on 52,158 parcels, 29,539 of them on a zip-conflict row (Hays 29,395, Caldwell 77, Travis 67). It had not written yet because the re-bake had not run. CTX-B7's gate blocks exactly those while preserving all 139,283 B6 recoveries.

2026-09-10: cad_property carries situs_city, situs_zip and land_acres (numeric), and fetchCountyCadPropertyRoll selected none of them before this card. Travis's 2025 roll has situs_city on ZERO of its 380,918 rows, which is why Travis's defect is 361,321 absences rather than disagreements.

Comparing addresses across CAD vintages by exact string is useless: Travis returns ZERO agreement in both directions purely because the 2025 StratMap drop and the 2026 PACS export format the same address differently. Normalise to the pre-first-comma segment, or better, compare a field with no formatting freedom.

Using a county-level key-stability percentage as the gate threshold. It needs a number nobody can defend, goes stale on the next acquisition, and cannot explain any individual parcel. The per-parcel ZIP corroboration is free, self-explaining on the row, and needs no constant.

The store is unchanged until the integration seat re-bakes and re-publishes the six counties. Until then 78,428 cities, 17,674 ZIPs and 103,913 acreages stay absent or refused -- and the 29,539 street overwrites stay un-written, which is the only reason the gate arrived in time.

The Hays dollar-path exposure (29,404 rows) is an operator ruling: re-declare 48209 to 2025, re-acquire a 2026 roll with a prop_id crosswalk, or extend CTX-B7's gate to fetchCountyCadPropertyRoll's dollar fields. No dollar-path change is in PR #652.
